key_insight: A 3D COMSOL opto-electro-thermal model shows that an n-ZnSe/p-SrScCu3Se4/p+-WSe2 heterostructure can achieve high photovoltaic performance when absorber width, doping, and defect density are optimized.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest SrScCu3Se4 is a promising quaternary chalcogenide absorber for high-efficiency, thermally aware solar-cell design and experimental prototyping.
method: Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and thermal loss
Parametric study of absorber width, acceptor concentration, and bulk defects
evidence_signal: Under optimized conditions, the device reached VOC = 1.02 V, JSC = 32.472 mA/cm2, FF = 88.212%, and PCE = 29.217%, with QE strongest in the visible spectrum.
watch_item: The near-infrared response and carrier-collection performance decline, and the thermally non-uniform heating highlights a need to validate these simulations experimentally under real device conditions.
paper_title: Computational analysis and performance optimization of SrScCu3Se4-based solar cells using COMSOL Multiphysics
